title: Angle Surgery Showdown: Goniotomy vs. Trabeculotomy
summary: A comprehensive clinical comparison of ab interno goniotomy and ab externo trabeculotomy for the surgical management of childhood glaucoma. These procedures aim to bypass the pathologically high resistance of the trabecular meshwork in primary congenital glaucoma (PCG).

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Both procedures are angle surgeries aimed at relieving obstruction in the trabecular meshwork (TM) for primary congenital glaucoma (PCG). Goniotomy involves an 'ab interno' approach, cutting the meshwork under direct visualization. Trabeculotomy involves an 'ab externo' approach, cannulating Schlemm's canal to rupture the TM.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Abandon Angle Surgery
content: Corneal opacification (Haab striae/edema) precluding visualization of the angle.
Uncontrolled IOP despite maximal angle intervention.
Evidence of secondary glaucoma (e.g., Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome or ICE).
Signs of angle closure or peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS).

content.explanation: If the cornea is CLOUDY, choose Trabeculotomy (Ab externo). If the cornea is clear, Goniotomy is the 'Gold' standard.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Success of goniotomy is highly dependent on corneal clarity; if corneal edema is severe, use an ab externo approach.
In trabeculotomy, ensure the trabeculotome is correctly placed in Schlemm’s canal by noting the resistance change.
Both surgeries carry a risk of transient hyphema; maintain the anterior chamber with viscoelastic (e.g., Healon).
Success is defined as normalized IOP without need for topical anti-glaucoma medication.

sections.title: Step-by-Step: Goniotomy Procedure
content: Step 1: Administer retrobulbar or general anesthesia; position patient head.
Step 2: Place Barkan goniotomy lens on the cornea to visualize the angle.
Step 3: Create a paracentesis; inject cohesive OVD (e.g., Provisc).
Step 4: Advance goniotomy knife across the AC to the nasal angle.
Step 5: Incise the TM in the anterior 1/3, sweeping 60-90 degrees.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: Examination Under Anesthesia (EUA) is mandatory for infants.
Measure horizontal corneal diameter (norm < 11mm in neonates; >12mm suspicious for buphthalmos).
Measure IOP (Tono-Pen or Perkins tonometer) - must be done quickly post-anesthesia induction.
Perform gonioscopy (critical to evaluate the insertion of the iris and presence of TM).
Axial length measurement (A-scan/IOLMaster) - compare to fellow eye or growth curves.
